questions.question: 6 labourers can finish a work in 16 days. 10 labourers are available, but the work is to be finished by 8 days. How many more labourers are to be called to finish the work in time?
questions.solution:
Given:

6 labourers can finish a work in 16 days.

Formula used:

Men × day = Total work

Calculation:

Total work = 6 × 16 = 96 unit.

According to the question, the work is to be finished by 8 days

Let the number of men required be a.

⇒ (10 + a) × 8 = 96

⇒ (10 + a) = 12

⇒ a = 2

∴ The number of extra labour required is 2.

questions.question: R, S and T can finish a work in 20, 15 and 10 days, respectively. R works on all days and S and T work on alternate days with T starting the work on the first day. In how many days is the work finished?
questions.solution:
Given:

R, S and T can finish a work in 20, 15 and 10 days, respectively

R works on all days and S and T work on alternate days with T starting the work on the first day.

Formula Used:

Efficiency = Total work/Time taken

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be 60 units(LCM of 20, 15, and 10).

Efficiency of R = 60/20 = 3 units/day

The efficiency of S = 60/15 = 4 units/day

Efficiency of T = 60/10 = 6 units/day

On the first day, R and T work = 9 units

On the second day, R and S work = 7 units

2 day's work → 16 units

6 day's work → 48 units

7 day's work → 57 units

The remaining work of 3 unit is done by R and S in = 3/7 days

Total Time = 7 + 3/7 = 52/7 days

**∴ In 52/7 days the work was finished.**

questions.question: ​A dishonest shopkeeper sells mangoes at Rs. 30/kg bought at Rs. 20/kg and he is giving 800 g instead of 1 kg. The shopkeeper's actual profit percentage is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Price ratio (CP : SP) = 20 : 30 = 2 : 3

Weight ratio (Actual : Claimed) = 800 : 1000 = 4 : 5

Effective CP : SP ratio = (2 × 4) : (3 × 5) = 8 : 15

Profit = 15 − 8 = 7 units.

Profit % = (7 ÷ 8) × 100 = 87.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 87.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price of 1 kg (1000 g) mangoes = Rs. 20

Selling price of 1 kg mangoes = Rs. 30

Actual weight given instead of 1 kg = 800 g

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0264c8255e9fb433aac2ba0121258579f1c91b8a8619c98277adb50b3e9924c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cost price of 1 g mango = 20 ÷ 1000 = Rs. 0.02

⇒ Actual cost price of 800 g mangoes = 800 × 0.02 = Rs. 16

⇒ The shopkeeper charges Rs. 30 for 800 g (claiming it as 1 kg).

⇒ Actual Selling price = Rs. 30

⇒ Profit = SP − Actual CP

⇒ Profit = 30 − 16 = Rs. 14

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ Actual CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (14 ÷ 16) × 100 = 87.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 87.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer sells goods using false weights, the actual cost price is based on the true weight delivered to the customer, while the selling price is based on the claimed weight.

Successive Ratio Method

The overall profit ratio can be derived by multiplying the individual price markup ratio (CP : SP) by the cheating weight ratio (Actual Weight : Claimed Weight).

Profit % Formula

Profit % = [(SP − Actual CP) ÷ Actual CP] × 100

questions.question: 4 men and 6 women can complete a work in 8 days, while 3 men and 7 women can complete it in 10 days. In how many days will 10 women complete it?
questions.solution:
Given:

4m + 6w = 8 days ----(1)

3m + 7w = 10 days ----(2)

Formula used:

Total work = Efficiency × days

Calculations:

By solving equations (1) and (2)

⇒ (4m + 6w) × 8 = (3m + 7w) × 10

⇒ 16m + 24w = 15m + 35w

⇒ 16m - 15m = 35w - 24w

⇒ m = 11w

⇒ m/w = 11/1

⇒ Total work = (4 × 11 + 6) × 8

⇒ Total work = 400 unit

⇒ Time taken by 10 woman = 400/10

⇒ Time taken by 10 woman = 40 days

∴ 10 women can complete the work in 40 days.

questions.question: The time required for a sum of money to amount to three times itself at 8% simple interest p.a. will be:
questions.solution:
Given:

Rate = 8%

Concept:

In simple interest, if a sum is Y and it becomes X times in a given year then interest = (X - 1) × Y

Formula used:

I = (P × R × T)/100

(Where, P = Principle, R = Rate, T = Times, and I = Simple interest)

Calculation:

Let's assume the principle is X then interest became at 8% is 2X, and time is T.

⇒ 2X = (X × 8 × T)/100

⇒ T = (2 × 100)/8 = 25 years

∴ Their required result will be 25 years.

questions.question: A boat covers a distance of 80 km downstream in 8 h while it takes 10 h to cover the same distance upstream. What is the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
Given:

The boat covers 80 km downstream distance in 8 hours

The boat covers 80 km upstream distance in 10 hours

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance / Time

Upstream speed = (x – y)

downstream speed = (x + y)

Where x and y are the speed of the boat and the speed of the stream

Calculation:

Let the speed of the boat be x km / hr

Speed of the boat upstream = 80 / 10 km / hr = 8 km / hr

Speed of the boat downstream = 80/8 = 10 km / hr

⇒ x – y = 8 ...(1)

⇒ x + y = 10 ....(2)

Solving both we get:

⇒ 2x = 18

⇒ x = 9

**The speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water is 9 km/hr**

questions.question:
Simplify the given expression.

(1+sin⁴ theta+cos⁴theta)/(cos² theta+sin⁴theta)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

(1+sin⁴ θ+cos⁴θ)/(cos² θ+sin⁴θ)

**Formula used:**

Sin² θ = (1 - cos² θ)

Cos² θ = (1 - sin² θ)

(a - b)² = a² + b² - 2ab

**Calculation:**

⇒ (1 + sin⁴ θ + cos ⁴ θ)/(cos² θ + sin⁴ θ)

⇒ {1 + sin⁴ θ + (1 - sin² θ)²}/(cos2 θ + sin4 θ)

⇒ {1 + sin4 θ + 1 + sin⁴ θ - 2 sin² θ)}/(cos2 θ + sin4 θ)

⇒ {2 + 2 sin 4 θ - 2 × (1 - cos² θ)}/(cos2 θ + sin4 θ)

⇒ {2 + 2 sin 4 θ - 2 + 2cos2 θ}/(cos2 θ + sin4 θ)

⇒ {2 sin 4 θ + 2cos2 θ}/(cos2 θ + sin4 θ)

⇒ 2 × {sin 4 θ + cos2 θ}(cos2 θ + sin4 θ)

⇒ 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Calculaton:

⇒ (1 + sin4 θ + cos 4 θ)/(cos2 θ + sin4 θ)

Put the value of θ = 90°

⇒ (1 + sin4 90° + cos 4 90°)/(cos2 90° + sin4 90°)

⇒ (1 + 1 + 0)/(0 + 1)

⇒ 2

∴ The correct answer is 2.

questions.question: Dharmendra can row 80 km upstream and 110 km downstream in 13 hours. Also, he can row 60 km upstream and 88 km downstream in 10 hours. What is the speed (in km/h) of the current?
questions.solution:
Given∶

Dharmendra can row 80 km upstream and 110 km downstream in 13 hours. 

He can row 60 km upstream and 88 km downstream in 10 hours. 

Formula used∶

Let u and v be the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the stream respectively.

Speed upstream = (u - v)

Speed downstream = (u + v)

Calculations∶

Let the speed of the boat upstream be U and the speed of the boat downstream be D

Time taken to travel 80 km upstream and 110 km downstream = 80/(u - v) + 110/(u + v)

⇒ 80/U + 110/D = 13 .......(1)

Time is taken to row 60 km upstream and 88 km downstream = 60/(u - v) + 88/(u + v)

⇒ 60/U + 88/D = 10 ............(2)

On equating (1) by 3 and (2) by 4 and subtracting equation (2) from equation (1):

3 × 110/D - 4 × 88/D = 39 - 40

⇒ (330 - 352)/D = - 1

⇒ - 22/D = - 1

D = 22 km/hr .....(3)

Putting equation (3) in equation (1).

⇒ 80/U + 110/22 = 13

⇒ 80/U + 5 = 13

⇒ 80/U = 13 - 5

⇒ U = 10 km/hr

Speed of the current = (D - U)/2

⇒ 12/2 = 6 km/hr

**The speed (in km/h) of the current is 6 km/hr.**

questions.question: In an examination a candidate had to sit for three papers A, B, and C. The candidate secured 75% marks in Paper A, 80% marks in Paper B, and 60% marks in Paper C. If the weightage assigned to Papers A, B, and C were 40%, 50% and 10%, respectively, then find the weighted percentage of marks obtained by the candidate, when all the three papers were taken together.
questions.solution:
**Given**

The candidate secured 75% marks in Paper A, 80% marks in Paper B, and 60% marks in Paper C

**Formula**

The weighted average of values is the sum of the weight times values divided by the sum of the weights.

**Calculation**

Let the maximum mark on each paper be 100.

Marks in Paper A = 75% of 100 = 75

Marks in Paper B = 80% of 100 = 80

Marks in Paper C = 60% of 100 = 60

Weightage of Paper A = 40% of 75 = 30

Weightage of Paper B = 50% of 80 = 40

Weightage of Paper C = 10% of 60= 6

The weighted percentage of marks obtained by the candidate

= (30 + 40 + 6)/100 × 100

= 76%

**The weighted percentage of marks obtained by the candidate is 76%.**

questions.question: A person marks his goods x% above the cost price and allows a discount of 12% on the marked price. If his profit is 10%, then the difference between x% and the profit percentage is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Discount = 12%

Profit = 10%

MP is x% above the CP

Formula Used:

P = SP – CP

D = MP – SP

SP = {(100 + P%)/100} × CP

SP = {(100 – D%)/100} × MP

Where P is Profit, CP is cost price, SP is selling price, MP is maximum retail price and D is discount.

Calculation:

SP = {(100 + 10)/100} × CP

⇒ SP = (110/100) × CP

MP = {(100 + x)/100} × CP

SP = 88% of MP

⇒ SP = 88/100 × {(100 + x)/100} × CP

⇒ (110/100) × CP = 88/100 × {(100 + x)/100} × CP

⇒ 110 = 88 × (100 + x)/100

⇒ 1000 = 8 × (100 + x)

⇒ 125 = 100 + x

⇒ x = 25.

The difference between x% and the profit percentage = 25 - 10

⇒ 15%

**The difference between x% and the profit percentage is 15%.**
